questions.q: What is the presumption of innocence?
questions.a: Everyone is innocent until proven guilty
w: Everyone is guilty until proven innocent
The police decide who is guilty
Only citizens have a right to a trial
questions.e: The Canadian justice system guarantees everyone due process under the law. Our system is founded on the presumption of innocence in criminal matters: everyone is innocent until proven guilty.

questions.q: What does 'rule of law' mean?
questions.a: Everyone is subject to the law, including the government, the police and judges
w: The Prime Minister is above the law
Only citizens must obey the law
Laws do not apply to rich people
questions.e: The rule of law is one of Canada's founding principles. Everyone, including the government, must follow the law. No one is above the law.

questions.q: What is 'due process'?
questions.a: The principle that the government must respect all the legal rights a person has under the law
w: The process of becoming a citizen
The order in which laws are passed
questions.e: Due process is the principle that the government must respect all of the legal rights a person is entitled to under the law.

questions.q: In Canada, the law applies equally to everyone, including judges, politicians and the police.
questions.e: Canada's legal system is based on the rule of law. Everyone is equal before the law, and no one is above it.

questions.q: What is the highest court in Canada?
w: The Court of Appeal of Ontario
questions.e: The Supreme Court of Canada is our country's highest court.

questions.q: Which court deals with matters concerning the federal government?
questions.e: The Federal Court of Canada deals with matters concerning the federal government.

questions.q: Where can people settle civil disputes involving small amounts of money?
questions.e: In most provinces there is a small claims court where you can settle disputes involving small amounts of money.

questions.q: In most provinces, what types of courts are there?
w: Only courts run by the federal police
questions.e: In most provinces there is an appeal court and a trial court, sometimes called the Court of King's Bench or the Supreme Court of the province.

questions.q: Courts in Canada settle disputes and decide on punishment for people who break the law.
questions.e: Courts settle disputes, and the police enforce the law. Judges decide cases fairly according to the law.

questions.q: Judges in Canada must follow the orders of the Prime Minister when deciding a case.
questions.e: Judges in Canada are independent. They decide cases according to the law and the evidence, not on the orders of politicians.

questions.q: What is the role of the police?
questions.a: To keep people safe and enforce the law
w: To decide who is guilty in court
questions.e: The police are there to keep people safe and to enforce the law. You can ask the police for help in all kinds of situations.

questions.q: Which police force enforces federal laws throughout Canada?
questions.e: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) enforces federal laws throughout Canada.

questions.q: In which provinces does the RCMP NOT serve as the provincial police?
questions.e: The RCMP serves as the provincial police in all provinces and territories except Ontario and Quebec, which have their own provincial police forces, and in some municipalities.

questions.q: What is the provincial police force of Ontario?
questions.e: Ontario and Quebec have their own provincial police forces: the Ontario Provincial Police and the Sûreté du Québec.

questions.q: What is the provincial police force of Quebec?
questions.e: Quebec's provincial police is the Sûreté du Québec.

questions.q: Many cities and towns in Canada have their own police forces.
questions.e: There are also municipal police forces in many cities and towns.

questions.q: In Canada, you can question the police about their service or conduct if you feel you need to.
questions.e: You can question the police about their service or conduct. Almost all police forces have a process for making complaints.

questions.q: It is a good idea to offer money to a police officer to avoid a ticket.
questions.e: Offering money to a police officer is bribery and is a serious crime in Canada.

questions.q: If you need legal help but cannot afford a lawyer, what may be available?
questions.a: Legal aid services, free or at low cost
w: Help from your Member of Parliament in court
A free lawyer from the Senate
questions.e: Lawyers can help with legal problems. In most areas there are legal aid services available free of charge or at low cost.

questions.q: In Canada, a person accused of a crime has the right to a lawyer.
questions.e: Legal Rights in the Charter include the right to be informed of the reason for arrest and the right to a lawyer.

questions.q: In Canada, what kind of law is used in Quebec for civil matters?
questions.a: Civil law based on the French civil code
questions.e: Quebec uses civil law based on the French civil code for private matters. The other provinces use English common law. Criminal law is the same everywhere in Canada.

questions.q: Criminal law is the same in every province of Canada.
questions.e: Criminal law is a federal responsibility, so the Criminal Code applies across all of Canada.

questions.q: Drinking and driving is a serious crime in Canada.
questions.e: Impaired driving is a serious crime in Canada. Laws are enforced to keep everyone safe.

questions.q: In Canada, family members may punish each other by violence if the family agrees.
questions.e: Violence, including in the family, is against the law. Everyone in Canada is protected by the law.

questions.q: In Canada, a person accused of a crime must prove they are innocent.
questions.e: The justice system is based on the presumption of innocence. A person is innocent until proven guilty.

questions.q: The RCMP is the provincial police in Ontario and Quebec.
questions.e: Ontario and Quebec have their own provincial police: the Ontario Provincial Police and the Sûreté du Québec.
